sweep.advice: None of these avoids the approved penetration cleanly: the 0.10 m lead-in leaves <0.11 m for bends before the wall, and over-the-top needs a 3.4 m lift. Keep the passed 130 mm cored opening with sleeve and seals; use a route only if a wall end is proven nearby by survey.

wonder_better.advice: Both geometry fixes are disproportionate for a DN50 air main compared with the already-passing Ø130 mm cored opening; keep the sleeved, fire-stopped penetration unless structure refuses it, in which case the services designer should choose between the over-top offset and the north-end route after surveying the wall ends.

best.title: Offset duct up 400 mm through girder opening

sweep.advice: Use the preformed opening, do not cut the transfer girder elsewhere. The mechanical modeller to make the offset and the structural engineer to confirm the opening use.
failures: Offset duct up 375 mm through girder opening: clearance with IfcBeam (+25 mm)

best.title: Offset tray up 250 mm through girder opening

sweep.advice: The through-opening offset is preferred as the smallest buildable fix; have the structural modeller confirm the opening is in the girder model and the electrical designer confirm bend radii and cable bend limits.

best.title: Offset main up 280 mm through girder opening

sweep.advice: Use the local offset through the provided opening; the structural reviewer owns the girder opening and the plumbing modeller owns the pipe offset. If the opening cannot be used, the main must be re-routed below the girder with fall checked.
